base_rate_triangulation._citation: One population (US organizations), one role per source: leak sites set the base rate, IRIS the floor. TEF = LEF ÷ susceptibility.
base_rate_triangulation._susceptibility_prior_note: P(initial access | attempt) 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.40 (judgment) × P(loss event | access) 0.50 / 0.57 / 0.76: Sophos State of Ransomware, share of attacks where data was encrypted, global 2022–2025 editions 76 / 70 / 50 / 56%, US 2025 57%. Product 0.10 / 0.17 / 0.30.

credential_tempo._citation: Derived from Recorded Future + IR report credential attack campaign patterns
credential_tempo._derivation: 300-500 publicly claimed ransomware victims per month × 2-4 under-counting = 1,000-3,000 campaigns/month (each campaign targets one organization); 50-55% credential-based; 5-15M organizations with exposed remote access (Shodan census). Ransomware.live shows ~740 claimed victims/month by attack date (Aug 2025-Jul 2026), which with 4× lands at the same high end.

exploitation_scanning._citation: GreyNoise 2025 Mass Exploitation Report + 2026 State of the Edge Report. IP-level malicious rate derived from cross-report comparison (13.5M tagged IPs in 2024 vs 3.8M malicious in H2 2025). Session-level malicious rate: 3.7% (18.3M/500M daily). Suspicious rate not published — would require API stats endpoint.
exploitation_scanning.grn_malicious_rate_derivation: IP-level: 3.8M malicious unique IPs / ~13.5M total tagged. Session-level: 18.3M malicious / 500M total daily = 3.7%. IP-level range used for ceiling calc.
exploitation_scanning.grn_suspicious_rate_note: Not published in either report. Requires Enterprise API stats endpoint or Research Community Access.
exploitation_scanning.campaign_ip_ratio_note: Judgment-based. React2Shell campaign (CVE-2025-55182) showed 73% of 3.9M sessions from just 2 JA4H fingerprints, suggesting high concentration. But campaign/IP ratios vary widely.
exploitation_scanning.poa_ransomware_note: Judgment-based. GreyNoise reports 28% of KEV CVEs tracked in 2024 associated with ransomware groups (Mass Exploitation 2025, p3).
exploitation_scanning.ransomware_proportion_note: Anchored to GreyNoise: 28% of KEV CVEs associated with ransomware (Mass Exploitation 2025). Range reflects uncertainty in mapping CVE-level data to scanning volume.

output_templates.one_sentence: Based on industry data, ransomware operators {attempt_verb} organizations matching your profile {recurrence} (range: {low} to {high}).

base_rate_lef._method: Leak-site recipe (the original operational-tempo method), on US organizations: US victims per year × under-reporting ÷ US firms in the revenue tier × the tier's share of victims.
base_rate_lef._n_us_note: ransomware.live victims by attack date, Aug 2025–Jul 2026 (12 complete months, the 2 latest left out for posting lag): 3,762 US among 8,405 with a country, unknown-country victims allocated pro rata. Recorded Future 2025: 3,784 US victims (cross-check). Live mode replaces n_us with the collected count.
base_rate_lef._underreporting_note: Share of events that reach a leak site = (1 − pay rate) × (1 − share by actors without leak sites); multiplier = 1 ÷ that share. Coveware Q4 2024–Q4 2025: pay rate 25 / ~30 / 26 / 23 / 20% (mean 24.8%), Lone Wolf actors 8 / 9 / 9 / 6 / 12% of cases (mean 8.8%). Low 1/((1−0.20)(1−0.06)), mode 1/((1−0.248)(1−0.088)), high 1/((1−0.35)(1−0.12)).
base_rate_lef._tier_note: US firms: Census SUSB 2022 detailed employment sizes (release 4/10/2025), each size band assigned to the revenue tier of its average receipts per firm: 1–39 employees < $10M, 40–299 $10M–100M, 300–2,499 $100M–1B. Victim shares: Coveware victim sizes (mean of Q4 2024 and Q4 2025; 1–10 employees 4% from Q2 2025; 10,000+ as the remainder: 4.0 / 33.8 / 36.3 / 16.6 / 9.3%), split log-uniformly at 40, 300 and 2,500 employees. From $100M up the rate is flat at the measured $100M–1B value (IRIS: 'organizations from $100M to $100B are pretty much all equally likely to be hit by ransomware'). Measured directly, $1B+ came out at about 26%/yr, above IRIS's upper bound, because Coveware's IR caseload over-represents large victims. Where the IRIS floor is higher (largest firms), the floor applies.
base_rate_lef._geography_note: The base rate counts US events over US firms, so the geography multiplier is relative to the US (US = 1.0).

floor_lef._citation: IRIS Ransomware Spotlight Table 3, lower bound: publicly reported ransomware events ÷ all D&B-registered US organizations in the tier. IRIS has no model under $10M (insufficient data), so that tier has no floor.
